title: LoRA
text: LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) fine-tunes a frozen pretrained weight matrix W0 by learning a low-rank update B times A scaled by alpha over r. B is initialized to zero so training starts exactly at the pretrained model. For a d_in by d_out matrix LoRA trains r times (d_in plus d_out) parameters instead of d_in times d_out. After training the update can be merged into W0 so inference has no extra latency.

title: QLoRA
text: QLoRA stores the frozen base model in 4-bit NormalFloat (NF4) and trains LoRA adapters on top in higher precision. It adds double quantization of the quantization constants and paged optimizers. QLoRA made it possible to fine-tune a 65B parameter model on a single 48 GB GPU.

title: DoRA
text: DoRA (Weight-Decomposed Low-Rank Adaptation) splits each weight into a magnitude vector and a direction. The magnitude is trained directly while the direction is updated with LoRA, which makes learning behave more like full fine-tuning.

title: GRPO
text: GRPO (Group Relative Policy Optimization) is a reinforcement learning algorithm introduced in the DeepSeekMath paper and used to train DeepSeek-R1. For each prompt it samples a group of completions and uses the group mean reward as the baseline, so it does not need a learned value network (critic). Advantages are rewards minus the group mean divided by the group standard deviation. It keeps PPO's clipped ratio and adds a KL penalty to a reference model.

title: DPO
text: Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) trains a model on pairs of chosen and rejected responses with a simple logistic loss on the difference of log-probability ratios against a frozen reference model. It optimizes the same KL-regularized objective as RLHF but without sampling or a reward model during training.

title: RL with verifiable rewards
text: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) uses programs to check answers, for example comparing a final math answer or running unit tests. Rule-based rewards are cheap and hard to game compared with learned reward models. This recipe produced the 2025 wave of open reasoning models.

title: Self-consistency
text: Self-consistency samples several reasoning paths at non-zero temperature and returns the most common final answer (majority vote). It is a simple way to trade more test-time compute for accuracy without a verifier.

title: Sparse autoencoders
text: A sparse autoencoder (SAE) is trained to reconstruct a model's internal activations through a wide hidden layer where only a few latents are active at a time. Its latents often correspond to human-interpretable features, which helps with monosemanticity research and mechanistic interpretability. TopK SAEs keep exactly k active latents per token.

title: Activation steering
text: Activation steering adds a direction to a model's residual stream during the forward pass to change its behavior, for example the mean difference between activations on two contrasting prompts, or the decoder direction of a sparse autoencoder feature.

title: Logit lens
text: The logit lens decodes intermediate residual stream states with the model's final layer norm and unembedding matrix, showing which next token the model is leaning toward at each layer.

title: Self-attention
text: Self-attention lets every token build its representation as a weighted average of value vectors from other tokens. The weights come from a softmax over scaled dot products of queries and keys. Causal masking prevents a token from attending to future positions in a language model.

title: KV cache
text: During autoregressive generation a transformer stores the keys and values of previous tokens in a KV cache so each new token only computes attention for itself. The cache grows linearly with sequence length and often dominates inference memory, which motivates grouped-query attention and cache quantization.

title: Retrieval-augmented generation
text: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) retrieves relevant passages from an external corpus and adds them to the prompt so the model can ground its answer in evidence. Retrieval quality is measured separately, for example with recall at k.

title: Sentence embeddings
text: Sentence embedding models such as Sentence-BERT map text to dense vectors so that semantically similar sentences are close in cosine similarity. Unlike TF-IDF they can match paraphrases that share no words.

title: TF-IDF and BM25
text: TF-IDF represents text by sparse term weights that grow with term frequency and shrink for words common across the corpus. BM25 is a refined lexical ranking function. Lexical methods are fast and strong for exact keywords, names and codes.

title: Model Context Protocol
text: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open standard introduced by Anthropic in November 2024 for connecting AI applications to tools and data. An MCP server exposes tools, resources and prompts; an MCP client inside the host application discovers and calls them over transports such as stdio or streamable HTTP, using JSON-RPC messages.

title: Tool use
text: With tool use the model is given JSON schemas describing functions. Instead of answering directly it can emit a tool call with arguments; the application executes the function and returns the result, and the loop continues until the model gives a final answer.

title: ReAct
text: ReAct interleaves reasoning traces with actions such as search or lookup, so the model can plan, act, observe the result and revise its plan. It is the conceptual ancestor of most modern agent loops.

title: Prompt injection
text: Prompt injection happens when text controlled by an attacker is interpreted by a model as instructions. Indirect prompt injection hides such instructions in web pages, emails or retrieved documents that an agent reads. Defenses include treating tool output as untrusted data, least-privilege tools, human confirmation for risky actions and output filtering.

title: Evals
text: Evals are test suites for model behavior. A good agent eval has fixed inputs, an automatic grader such as exact match, a regex or an LLM judge, and tracks pass rate over time so regressions are caught before deployment.

title: Honey bee waggle dance
text: Honey bee foragers communicate the direction and distance of flowers with the waggle dance. The angle of the waggle run relative to vertical encodes the direction relative to the sun and the duration encodes distance.

title: Honey
text: Bees make honey by evaporating nectar and adding enzymes. A single worker bee produces roughly one twelfth of a teaspoon of honey in her lifetime. Ripe honey has a water content below about 18 percent which prevents fermentation.
